primary_source_findings: The upstream realtime service admits input_audio_buffer.append, input_audio_buffer.commit, output_audio_buffer.clear, session.update, conversation.item.create, response.create and response.cancel as client events.
The upstream service emits session, speech-start/stop, conversation-item, transcription, response audio/text, function-call arguments and response.done events.
The upstream event model inspected in this turn does not list conversation.item.truncate or conversation.item.truncated.

Upstream response cancellation uses a response cancellation path, but response.cancel/output buffer clear alone does not prove server conversation history is truncated to exactly what the user actually heard.

The OpenAI-compatible STT backend keeps VAD, turn, session, conversation and response handling inside speech-to-speech and may progressively re-upload accumulated utterance audio; this is an integration/latency and authority-boundary risk that must be measured rather than assumed away.

observed: Barge-in transitions queued output to cancelled and started/heard output to interrupted.
Barge-in revokes commit eligibility and fences outstanding tool ownership.
Only fully heard completed output is commit-eligible.
VoiceOutcome result references require fully heard commit-eligible output.
f2_semantic_requirement.compatibility_consequence: A protocol-compatible local server must preserve heard-versus-unheard history/commit semantics, not merely stop generation or clear playback.

coordination_negative.observed: Commit 91882abf7b0860279cce97ce1b88e1ac0ae9f719 adds a regression expecting huggingface/speech-to-speech aliases and stable semantic key 8c53f25e..., while the current fetched t7_semantic_claim.py still lacks those subject aliases.
coordination_negative.consequence: Do not create a material semantic claim by hand or invent a new alias. Reconcile compiler source plus test first, then acquire the canonical create-only semantic claim if still unowned.

hypothesis: The local cascade can preserve much of the existing realtime transport/client boundary while Frankenstein retains canonical VoiceIntent, VoiceSessionCapsule, UnifiedDB, tool/effect and heard-state authority outside the speech server.
counterhypotheses: Missing conversation.item.truncate semantics cause the server-side assistant context to retain speech that the user never heard after barge-in.
The server's internal conversation/session state becomes a competing authority rather than a transient speech transport projection.
Response cancellation stops generation but fails to revoke already-buffered or already-contextualized unheard assistant content.
Progressive accumulated-utterance STT adds unacceptable compute/latency under the intended local hardware envelope.
The apparent OpenAI-Realtime compatibility is insufficient for Frankenstein's exact tool, cancellation, event-order and close semantics.
next_exact_action: First reconcile the semantic-claim compiler/test drift without inventing identity. Then, if the canonical semantic key can be acquired create-only, run one bounded protocol-compatibility falsifier against a pinned speech-to-speech revision: exercise session.update, input append/commit, response.create/cancel, output clear, tool call/result continuation, confirmed barge-in and heard/unheard rollback. The highest-information discriminator is whether server-side conversation context after interruption contains any assistant text/audio beyond the F2 heard boundary. Run network-blocked local inference only after the protocol gate is valid.
